$comment: Content's heights are placed on the project's ground only where the vertical datum the content
states is the one the ground was built in, and are refused by name otherwise: a frame names its
datum as well as its CRS and its unit, and this is the named skip HPS-53 gives a file in another
frame (MPB 1.8.0).
The Revit host is an order-frame host: within one bundle every height it places is in the
delivery's datum, the ground's included. Across two it is not. From 1.8.0 a US order's content in
the delivery CRS is NAVD88 (GEOID18), and before it every bundle was EGM2008. A re-import of a
1.8.0 rebuild keeps the ground an earlier build made, so the ground records its datum when it is
built and each height step compares the datum its own content states with that record. A
difference is a skip that places nothing and shifts no height; the published offset between the
two datums is one number for the whole site and is not this host's to apply.
Unstated compares by version, never by key. Every bundle before 1.8.0 was EGM2008, so content
from before 1.8.0 stating none, and a ground recording none, both read as EGM2008; a stated datum
outranks that on either side. Content that states none on a 1.8.0 manifest is a producer's gap and
is refused rather than assumed to match. A datum no reader knows fails closed, naming the value,
even against the same string. Datums are compared verbatim.
`manifest` is one embedded 1.8.0 document. Each row lays its own members over it before it is
parsed -- `root` over the document, `treePoints` over `landcover.tree_points`; a value sets a
member and null removes it -- and plans it, so the statement the tree step carries is proven
through the parser and the planner, not beside them. `ground` is what the project's ground of
this order records: `vertical_datum` is the datum its stamp names, or null for a ground recording
none (built from a manifest before 1.8.0, or by a build of the host before the record). `outcome`
is `placeable` or `unplaceable`; `errorContains` is asserted on an `unplaceable` row only.
The unknown and case-folded datums sit on the ground's side because that is where a free string
reaches this host: the ground records `hosts.revit.georeference.vertical_datum`, which the format
leaves a free string, while `landcover.tree_points.vertical_datum` is an enum of the two datums
and every row here validates against the schema its version names.
The base row is a US order on its first import: everything NAVD88, the ground included. The
tree points stand for every height step, since what is compared is the step's statement and the
ground's record, whichever file the statement came from; the document's site is the corpus's usual
one, and nothing in this table reads where it is.

rows.name: stated and equal: NAVD88 trees on a ground built in NAVD88 are placed
unstated against unstated: trees from before 1.8.0 on a ground recording no datum are placed
a ground recording no datum reads as EGM2008, so trees stating EGM2008 are placed
a ground recording no datum against trees stating NAVD88 is unplaceable: the re-import this case exists for
a stated pair that differs is unplaceable and not shifted
a stated datum outranks the version: 1.7.0 trees stating NAVD88 on a ground recording none are unplaceable
the datum is compared verbatim: a ground recording a spelling that differs only in case is another datum
a datum no reader knows fails closed, naming it: a ground recording one places nothing on it
trees stating no datum on a 1.8.0 manifest are unplaceable, not read as an older bundle
